mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer demand, proxied by HOUST, leads to higher corporate earnings expectations and thus a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns fail to outperform a 5-day rolling average by more than 0.5 percentage points in 60% of periods when HOUST is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in employment, measured by PAYEMS, reduces labor market uncertainty and boosts investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In regimes with PAYEMS growth > +2% monthly, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% triggers a risk-off channel, lowering equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: normalization phase after rate hike cycle
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for 30 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand or supply shocks that reduce corporate earnings growth expectations, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows a U-shaped pattern with 20-day forward returns turning positive in >70% of recovery phases (3 consecutive months of improvement).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) creates a dual positive momentum effect that drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS show double-digit monthly growth, 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a single-demand proxy (RSAFS) by >1 percentage point (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals labor market tightening that accelerates corporate investment and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to beat the 5-day average by more than 0.8 percentage points in 40% of post-tightening episodes (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2%) lowers real interest rates and shifts capital into growth stocks, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive months of FEDFUNDS < 2%, 5-day forward returns average zero with a p-value > 0.1 in a two-sample test against a neutral baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with falling consumer confidence (CPIAUCSL) creates a dual supply-demand shock that depresses earnings expectations and yields negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL falls > 5% in a quarter while INDPRO declines > -3%, 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).
